title: Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all death row inmates in California
summary: Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and a rumored presidential candidate, moved to commute the death sentences of 548 inmates in California for one of his last acts as governor.

image.caption: Gavin Newsom's term ends in 2027Image: Steven Senne/AP/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: California Governor Gavin Newsom said Thursday that he will change all death sentences in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

"I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us," Newsom said in a letter to Californians.
There are 548 people on death row in California.
Newsom added in the letter that he has long opposed death penalty and issued a moratorium on executions in 2019.
Newsom can commute about 40% of the death sentences with the stroke of a pen, but the rest will require the high court's approval to be finalized, according to the Los Angeles Times.
